query: FeCoNi is an fcc alloy with high saturation magnetization and a low coercive field. Earlier studies examined the high-entropy alloys FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt, but both exhibited soft ferromagnetism. A qualifying high-entropy alloy must have an almost equiatomic multicomponent composition and configurational entropy of at least 1.0R. Subject to these constraints, what single intervention could produce a FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloy with greater coercivity than the prior derivatives? Present one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the outcome relative to an appropriate FeCoNi-based baseline, defines the conditions over which it should apply, cites supporting observations from earlier work, and proposes a discriminating experiment with an explicit falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: The addition of Cr to the FeCoNi alloy will produce a high-entropy alloy with greater coercivity than the prior derivatives.
generation.conditions: Equiatomic multicomponent composition and configurational entropy of at least 1.0R
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a two-phase mixture of ordered B2 and disordered BCC solid solution
generation.mechanism: Replacement of Co by Cr in the FeCoNi alloy results in a substantial reduction in saturation magnetization and increase in coercivity.
generation.uncertainty: The exact amount of Cr to be added and the resulting microstructure and magnetic properties of the alloy

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare FeCoNi and FeCoNiCr alloys with equiatomic composition and measure their coercivity and microstructure.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the coercivity of the FeCoNiCr alloy is not greater than that of the FeCoNi alloy, the hypothesis is falsified.

Own digest: Influence of Cr Substitution and Temperature on Hierarchical Phase Decomposition in the AlCoFeNi High Entropy Alloy

Abstract: While the AlCoFeNi high entropy alloy exhibits a single ordered B2 phase at high temperature, both the substitution of ferromagnetic Co with antiferromagnetic Cr, and lower annealing temperatures lead to a tendency for this system to decompose into a two-phase mixture of ordered B2 and disordered BCC solid solution. The length scale of this decomposition is determined by the combination of composition and annealing temperature, as demonstrated in this investigation by comparing and contrasting AlCoFeNi with the AlCo0.5Cr0.5FeNi alloy. The resulting phase stability has been rationalized based on solution thermodynamic predictions.
